issues.legal_issue: Becoming an occupant of forest land does not, without the required survey settlement or concession, give the former holder a right to cut and remove trees from that land.
material_facts: The former holders’ jagirs were abolished, and they became occupants of forest lands under the abolition law.
The villages containing the forest lands had not been surveyed or settled.
The former holders claimed a right, as occupants, to cut and remove trees, including reserved species.
issues.conclusion: The former holders acquired occupancy rights in the forest lands, but those rights did not include a right to cut and remove the trees. Because the villages had not been surveyed and settled, the government’s rights to the trees could not be deemed conceded to the occupants.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3 and 5(1)(b) of the Bombay Merged Territories and Areas (Jagirs Abolition) Act, 1953 extinguished jagir rights except as expressly preserved and conferred occupancy rights in the land. Under section 40 of the Bombay Land Revenue Code, the government’s rights to trees are deemed conceded to occupants in the circumstances specified for surveyed and settled villages or land occupied after settlement; no such concession follows where the required survey settlement has not occurred. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: appeal_from_writ_order_recognizing_tree_cutting_rights and former_holder_became_land_occupant and land_is_forest_land and village_not_surveyed_or_settled

predicates.appeal_from_writ_order_recognizing_tree_: The proceeding is an appeal from an order allowing a writ petition that recognized a claimed right to cut and remove trees.
predicates.former_holder_became_land_occupant: A person who formerly held rights under an abolished tenure became an occupant of land under the applicable transition law.
predicates.land_is_forest_land: The land at issue is forest land bearing trees.
predicates.village_not_surveyed_or_settled: The village containing the land had not undergone the survey settlement required for a deemed concession of tree rights.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a claimed tree-cutting right on forest land, and a former holder became an occupant but the village was not surveyed and settled, the occupant does not automatically have the right to cut or remove the trees.

issues.legal_issue: A provision vesting specified tree rights in the government does not impliedly preserve all other tree rights for former tenure holders when the abolition law extinguishes their rights unless expressly saved.
material_facts: The abolition law extinguished the former holders’ rights arising from their jagirs unless a right was expressly preserved.
The law vested specified rights to trees in the government.
The law expressly preserved certain rights concerning mines and mineral products but contained no corresponding express preservation of the former holders’ rights to trees.
The former holders argued that the government’s specified tree rights impliedly left all other tree rights with them.
issues.conclusion: The specified vesting of tree rights in the government did not imply that the former holders retained all other tree rights. Their rights were extinguished because no express provision saved them.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 of the Bombay Merged Territories and Areas (Jagirs Abolition) Act, 1953 extinguished jagirdar rights except where the Act expressly provided otherwise. Section 9 vested specified tree rights in the State Government but did not expressly preserve other tree rights for jagirdars. Section 10’s express preservation of rights to mines and mineral products supported the conclusion that the absence of a comparable provision for trees was significant. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.appeal_concerns_former_holder_tree_right: The proceeding is an appeal concerning tree rights claimed by a person whose former tenure was abolished.
predicates.abolition_extinguished_former_tenure_rig: The legal change abolished the former tenure and extinguished its incidents unless expressly preserved.
predicates.government_was_given_specified_tree_righ: The governing law vested specified rights to trees in the government.
predicates.no_express_saving_of_former_holder_tree_: The governing law did not expressly preserve the former holder’s claimed tree rights, although it expressly preserved other specified rights.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns tree rights claimed by a former tenure holder, and the law extinguishes former-tenure rights unless expressly saved while vesting specified tree rights in the government, other rights are not impliedly saved for the former holder if no express saving applies.
